description: Improve debuggability when POST /factory-sessions inspects a readable folder but cannot recognize a runnable factory because runtime config loading fails during discovery. Preserve the real failure in logs and API classification, and show actionable inline dashboard diagnostics instead of suggesting factory initialization.

context.customerAsk: Improve debuggability for factory session target discovery so readable folders with broken factory configs do not collapse into not_runnable or init-new-factory behavior. Log the real load failure, return a structured validation-style API error, and update the dashboard to show actionable issues instead of suggesting factory initialization.
context.problem: Today a runtime config load failure during POST /factory-sessions discovery can be silently suppressed into not_runnable or validate-only initsNewFactory: true. That hides the real failure from operators, prevents API consumers from distinguishing broken configs from empty folders, and can mislead dashboard users into initializing a new factory over an existing broken one.
context.solution: Preserve config-load failures as a first-class discovery outcome in the backend, emit structured operator logs, shape a safe validation-style BAD_REQUEST API response with a stable failure code and issue targets, and update the dashboard launch flow to render accessible inline diagnostics while keeping empty-folder initialization behavior unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria: POST /factory-sessions preserves readable-folder runtime config load failures as a distinct classification rather than collapsing them into not_runnable or initNewFactory behavior.
The backend emits structured error logs for discovery-time config load failures with submitted folder path, probed target path, and target identity when known.
Validate-only and session-open discovery requests classify the same broken folder the same way while preserving existing runnable-factory and genuine empty-folder behavior.
The public API returns a structured BAD_REQUEST response with a stable config-load-failed code, safe summary message, and issue targets for the affected factory subject.
The dashboard renders an inline accessible error panel for config-load-failed responses and does not offer init-new-factory actions or create a failed session tab for that case.
Typecheck, lint, generated-artifact checks, and targeted backend, API, and UI tests pass.

userStories.title: Log config load failures during target discovery
userStories.description: As an operator, I want discovery-time config load failures recorded in structured logs so that I can tell why a readable folder was rejected without reproducing under a debugger.
acceptanceCriteria: When /factory-sessions discovery probes a readable candidate and runtime config loading fails, the backend emits a structured error log instead of silently suppressing the failure.
The log includes the submitted folder path, the probed factory target path, target identity when known, and a safe summary of the underlying load failure.
The log is emitted for both validate-only and session-open discovery paths and is not emitted for successful discovery.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Return structured API diagnostics for broken factory config loads
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want a structured validation-style error for broken factory config loads so that I can distinguish them from missing folders, unreadable folders, and genuine init-new-factory cases.
acceptanceCriteria: When a readable folder exists but runtime config loading fails during /factory-sessions discovery, the API returns BAD_REQUEST rather than initsNewFactory: true or a generic not_runnable outcome.
The response includes a stable public failure code that is distinct from missing, unreadable, non-directory, and not-runnable classifications.

The response includes a safe top-level message and structured issue targets that identify the affected factory subject and summarize the load failure without exposing stack traces or unsafe internals.
The same broken folder yields the same failure classification and issue payload shape for validate-only and session-open requests.
Validate-only requests for genuinely empty readable folders still return init-new-factory metadata rather than the new config-load-failed error.
If the public API shape changes, the authored OpenAPI fragments, bundled contract, and generated Go and TypeScript clients are updated together.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Show actionable inline diagnostics in the dashboard
userStories.description: As a dashboard user, I want broken-factory launch failures shown inline with actionable details so that I understand what needs fixing without being sent down the new-factory path.
acceptanceCriteria: When the dashboard receives the new config-load-failed response from /factory-sessions, it renders an inline error panel on the current launch flow instead of treating the folder as an init-new-factory candidate.
The panel shows the top-level message and the structured issue list returned by the API, with readable text and semantics that do not rely on color alone.
The UI does not create, switch to, or partially initialize a new session tab for the failed request.
Existing init-new-factory affordances remain available only for genuine empty-folder validation responses.
The failure presentation works on desktop and mobile widths and preserves keyboard-readable access to the returned issues.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill

userStories.title: Keep validate and open-session flows aligned across runnable, empty, and broken folders
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want validation and open-session discovery to classify the same folder the same way so that backend, API, and UI behavior do not diverge across preflight and launch paths.
acceptanceCriteria: The same broken factory folder yields the same config-load-failed classification whether the request is validate-only or a direct session-open attempt.
A runnable factory folder remains discoverable and openable in both validate-only and session-open flows without the new error classification.
A truly empty readable folder still returns init-new-factory discovery metadata only in validate-only flows and does not regress into a broken-config classification.

Regression coverage proves the distinction between runnable-factory, empty-folder, and broken-config cases at the service/API layer and for the dashboard launch behavior that depends on those outcomes.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
